"""Public reproduction for the NMR peak-set encoding workflow.

The script encodes the same spectra with different batch padding lengths and
checks the physical consistency conditions described in `paper.md`:

- an encoded spectrum must not depend on how many dummy padding rows were
  appended to batch the peak list;
- the report records how much the encoded spectrum responds when a real
  observed peak changes, without applying a task-specific public lower bound.

It writes a machine-readable report under `outputs/` and exits with:

- 0: `post_fix_success`
- 1: `pre_fix_expected_failure`
- 2: `runner_failure`
"""

    输出: (B, L_unique, d_model) 的峰特征编码
    核心优势:

    - 置换不变性（permutation-invariant）
    - 支持任意层数的ISAB编码

        Q = self.ln1(Q)
        K = self.ln1(K)
        q = self.fc_q(Q).view(Q.size(0), Q.size(1), self.num_heads, self.dim_V // self.num_heads)
        k = self.fc_k(K).view(K.size(0), K.size(1), self.num_heads, self.dim_V // self.num_heads)
        v = self.fc_v(K).view(K.size(0), K.size(1), self.num_heads, self.dim_V // self.num_heads)
        q = q.permute(0, 2, 1, 3)  # (B, H, Lq, D/H)
        k = k.permute(0, 2, 3, 1)  # (B, H, D/H, Lk)
        v = v.permute(0, 2, 1, 3)  # (B, H, Lk, D/H)
        att = torch.matmul(q, k) / math.sqrt(self.dim_V // self.num_heads)
        if mask is not None:

            mask = mask.unsqueeze(1).unsqueeze(1)
            att = att.masked_fill(mask == 0, -1e9)
        att = torch.softmax(att, dim=-1)

        out = out.view(out.size(0), out.size(1), self.dim_V)  # (B, Lq, D)
        out = self.fc_o(out)

The data pipeline confirms the convention: `features.py:42` documents "mask where 1=valid and 0=pad", and MAB masks out `mask == 0` positions. The bug is that both encoders pass the **inverted** `pad_mask = ~mask` (1=pad) to the ISAB/PMA attention layers, which causes MAB to mask out the *real* peaks and attend only to padding.

This single inversion explains both symptoms:
- **Padding instability (1H)**: padding rows are attended, and the exact (unpadded) pass uses `mask=None` so all real peaks are attended — different results.
- **Zero sensitivity (both)**: real peaks are masked out, so moving a peak has no effect; the global repr only sees constant padding tokens.

The repair is complete and verified.

## Root cause

A single inverted mask convention in `source/src/model.py`. The `MAB` attention block masks out keys where `mask == 0` (i.e. it expects **1=valid / 0=pad**), which matches the rest of the pipeline (`features.py`, `FusionLayer`, T5 `attention_mask` all use 1=valid). But both encoders computed `pad_mask = ~mask` (1=pad) and passed *that* to the ISAB/PMA layers. The result: attention **masked out the real peaks and attended only to padding**.

This explains both reported symptoms exactly:
- **Padding instability (1H)**: the unpadded pass used `mask=None` (attend all real peaks) while the padded pass attended the padding rows → different outputs. (13C looked stable only because `_process_peaks` pre-canonicalizes the input into a fixed buffer, masking the symptom.)
- **Zero sensitivity (both modalities)**: real peaks were masked out, so moving one had no effect — the global representation only saw constant padding tokens.

## Fix

Three focused changes in `source/src/model.py`, preserving the architecture (stacked ISAB, PMA, learnable pad tokens, projections), signatures, and input layouts:
- `SetTransformerPeakEncoder.forward` (`source/src/model.py:224`): pass the 1=valid `valid_mask` to ISAB/PMA instead of the inverted `pad_mask`.
- `SetTransformer1HNMRPeakEncoder.forward` (`source/src/model.py:378`): pass the 1=valid `mask.bool()` to ISAB/PMA instead of the inverted `pad_mask` (pad-token replacement still uses `pad_mask` correctly).
- `MAB.forward` (`source/src/model.py:52`): documented the 1=keep / 0=mask-out convention to prevent regression.

## Verification

- `python reproduce.py` → `post_fix_success`, 24/24 checks pass; sensitivity now nonzero (≈1e-3–1e-2, was 0.0); max padding diff 3.6e-7 (float32 noise).
- A generality stress suite (4 encoder configs × 6 seeds, 240 padding trials) confirmed: padding invariance of global + per-peak features across `pad_to ∈ {exact, +1, +3/+5, +11/+13, max_peaks}`; permutation invariance of the pooled representation and equivariance of per-peak features; nonzero sensitivity; finiteness; batched mixed-length spectra matching per-sample encodings; and 13C duplicate-ppm intensity counting.
